question: I bought two frocks for ₹1,200. I sold the first frock at a loss of 7% and the second at a profit of 23%. If I made neither a loss nor a profit overall, find the purchase price (in ₹) of the first frock.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a no profit no loss transaction, the absolute loss amount on the first item equals the absolute profit amount on the second.

Ratio of CP₁ to CP₂ = Profit% on 2nd : Loss% on 1st = 23 : 7

Total CP parts = 23 + 7 = 30 parts → ₹1200

Value of 1 part = 1200 ÷ 30 = ₹40

CP of the first frock = 23 parts × ₹40 = ₹920

**∴ The correct answer is ₹920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price (CP) of two frocks = ₹1200

Loss on the first frock = 7%

Profit on the second frock = 23%

Net overall profit or loss = 0%

**Method Used:**

We can use the Alligation method to find the ratio of their Cost Prices directly.

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price of the first frock be x and the second frock be y.

⇒ Total CP = x + y = 1200

Since there is no net profit or loss, the loss on the first frock exactly equals the profit on the second frock.

⇒ 7% of x = 23% of y

⇒ (7 ÷ 100) × x = (23 ÷ 100) × y

⇒ 7x = 23y

⇒ x ÷ y = 23 ÷ 7

⇒ The ratio of their cost prices is 23 : 7

⇒ Total parts in the ratio = 23 + 7 = 30 parts

⇒ 30 parts = 1200

⇒ 1 part = 1200 ÷ 30 = 40

⇒ Cost price of the first frock (x) = 23 parts = 23 × 40 = 920

**∴ The correct answer is ₹920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Principle

When a complete transaction yields overall zero profit and zero loss, the absolute loss incurred on the first item perfectly offsets the absolute profit gained on the second item. Thus, Loss Amount = Profit Amount.

Alligation on Profit and Loss

Alligation can be effectively applied on profit (+%) and loss (−%) rates. The middle value represents the net percent change. The ratio found at the bottom always denotes the ratio of the base quantities, which in this case is their Cost Prices (CP).

Basic Profit and Loss Formulae

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100
